clauses.mechanism: completion_of_task: self-executing termination of the Executive Order 12722 emergency, revocation of Executive Orders 12722, 12724, 12734, 12743, 12751 and 12817, and amendment of Executive Order 13290, effective 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time July 30, 2004 under section 10
clauses.reason: The preamble, read with section 10, did three one-time things at the order's effective time. It terminated the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12722; it revoked Executive Orders 12722, 12724, 12734, 12743, 12751 and 12817 as based on that emergency; and it amended Executive Order 13290 so that its authorities rest on the emergency declared in Executive Order 13303 as expanded in Executive Order 13315. Section 10 makes the order effective at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 30, 2004 (the order is dated July 29, 2004 and was published July 30, 2004 at 69 FR 46055), so these commands were performed on 2004-07-30 and are exhausted by performance. Their results survive: the six revoked orders stay revoked, and the amended text of Executive Order 13290 is carried by the clause for section 3, which is decided separately as operative. The end date is the stated effective date (a fixed effective time, not an until-date, so no inclusive or exclusive reading arises). The 2010 Treasury rulemaking at 75 FR 55463 describes the same performance (Executive Order 13350 terminated the Executive Order 12722 emergency and revoked that order, Executive Order 12724 and the later orders based on it).

research_rationale:
Identity and text: the held original is the Federal Register text (69 FR 46055 (Federal Register, July 30, 2004)) of Executive Order 13350 of July 29, 2004, Termination of Emergency Declared in Executive Order 12722 With Respect to Iraq and Modification of Executive Order 13290, Executive Order 13303, and Executive Order 13315. I read the held text in full; its title, number, date and Federal Register pages agree with the register row and the packet. The held text is the Federal Register text of 69 FR 46055 (13 PDF pages; the inventoried operative text ends at section 10 and the Annex pages that follow list the blocked persons, which section 2 incorporates). The clause inventory has 11 clauses and matches the text I read. Status YES is retained on the established original_plus_bounded_search route: the held original; no own-terms end (the order has no sunset, expiry or self-revocation); every held later instrument that names the order is either attached as a later event or explained in the earlier-end check as not acting on it; the national-emergency predicate; and the three bounded searches. Emergency predicate: The order rests on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13303 of May 22, 2003 and expanded in Executive Order 13315 of August 28, 2003. The held presidential continuation notices selected in the packet run from 2005-05-19 to 2026-05-04 (16 notices, each naming the order by number); the latest, the notice of 2026-05-04 (91 FR 25071; FR Doc. 2026-09176), continues the emergency beyond May 22, 2026, so the emergency was in force on 2026-10-14. The packet's selectable notices omit the years 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012 between the first and last held year; I do not rely on those years, and the latest notice itself continues an existing emergency. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes in the packet: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, statute text and editorial notes, edition current through 2026-10-09, so laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected), current-law:ecfr (eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk XML, 49 titles read) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes, 6942 catalog records, plus operative sentences in 16784 saved order texts). Each is marked complete with no coverage warning; they are machine leads, and I read the held later texts myself. Cut-off: every clause is decided as of 2026-10-14. The Federal Register text of the order was read from the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF held at the original path; I confirmed identity from the heading, number, date and FR pages, not from page images.
